title.en: State how O2 and CO2 are carried in blood

say.en: Oxygen barely dissolves in water, yet every cell in your toes receives it within a minute. The secret is a red protein that picks oxygen up in the lungs and drops it in the tissues. In this lesson: State how O2 and CO2 are carried in blood.
Interpret the oxygen dissociation curve.
Write the carbonic anhydrase reaction.

body.en: About 97 per cent of O2 is carried by red blood cells and only about 3 per cent dissolved in plasma. Haemoglobin is a red, iron-containing pigment in RBCs; each molecule can carry at most four molecules of O2, forming oxyhaemoglobin. Binding depends mainly on pO2, and also on pCO2, H+ concentration and temperature. A plot of percentage saturation of haemoglobin against pO2 is the sigmoid *oxygen* dissociation curve. In the alveoli — high pO2, low pCO2, lower H+ and lower temperature — oxyhaemoglobin forms; in the tissues — low pO2, high pCO2, high H+ and higher temperature — oxygen dissociates. Every 100 mL of oxygenated blood delivers about 5 mL of O2 to the tissues.
body.kn: ಸುಮಾರು 97% ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕವನ್ನು ಕೆಂಪು ರಕ್ತಕಣಗಳ ಹಿಮೋಗ್ಲೋಬಿನ್ ಮತ್ತು 3% ಪ್ಲಾಸ್ಮಾ ಸಾಗಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂದು ಹಿಮೋಗ್ಲೋಬಿನ್ ಅಣು ಗರಿಷ್ಠ ನಾಲ್ಕು O2 ಅಣುಗಳನ್ನು ಹೊರುತ್ತದೆ. ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕ ವಿಘಟನಾ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆ S ಆಕಾರದ್ದು. 100 ಮಿ.ಲೀ ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕಯುಕ್ತ ರಕ್ತ ಸುಮಾರು 5 ಮಿ.ಲೀ O2 ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Plot percent saturation of haemoglobin against pO2 and you get an S-shaped, sigmoid curve.
High pCO2, more H+ ions and higher temperature in the tissues shift the curve right, so oxygen is let go more easily.
About 97 percent of oxygen rides on haemoglobin; each haemoglobin carries at most four O2 molecules.
Carbonic anhydrase in red cells makes bicarbonate in the tissues and reverses the reaction at the alveoli.
The teacher plots the oxygen dissociation curve, shows the right shift and writes the bicarbonate reaction.

caption.en: Haemoglobin saturation plotted against pO2 is sigmoid. In the lungs (high pO2, low pCO2, less H+, lower temperature) oxyhaemoglobin forms; in the tissues (low pO2, high pCO2, more H+, higher temperature) the curve shifts right and O2 is released. Normally 100 mL of oxygenated blood gives about 5 mL of O2 to the tissues.
caption.kn: pO2 ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಹೀಮೋಗ್ಲೋಬಿನ್ ಸಂತೃಪ್ತಿ ಸಿಗ್ಮಾ ಆಕಾರದ ವಕ್ರ. ಅಂಗಾಂಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ (ಕಡಿಮೆ pO2, ಹೆಚ್ಚು pCO2, ಹೆಚ್ಚು H+, ಹೆಚ್ಚು ತಾಪ) ವಕ್ರ ಬಲಕ್ಕೆ ಸರಿದು O2 ಬಿಡುಗಡೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. 100 mL ರಕ್ತ ಸುಮಾರು 5 mL O2 ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Nearly 20–25 per cent of CO2 is carried by haemoglobin as carbamino-haemoglobin, about 70 per cent as bicarbonate and about 7 per cent dissolved in plasma. RBCs contain a very high concentration of the enzyme carbonic anhydrase (plasma has a minute amount), which speeds up the reversible reaction below. At the tissues, where pCO2 is high, bicarbonate forms; at the alveoli, where pCO2 is low, the reaction reverses and CO2 is released. Every 100 mL of deoxygenated blood delivers about 4 mL of CO2 to the alveoli.
body.kn: ಸುಮಾರು 20–25% CO2 ಕಾರ್ಬಮಿನೋ-ಹಿಮೋಗ್ಲೋಬಿನ್ ಆಗಿ, ಸುಮಾರು 70% ಬೈಕಾರ್ಬನೇಟ್ ಆಗಿ ಮತ್ತು 7% ಪ್ಲಾಸ್ಮಾದಲ್ಲಿ ಕರಗಿ ಸಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಕೆಂಪು ರಕ್ತಕಣಗಳಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಕಾರ್ಬಾನಿಕ್ ಅನ್‌ಹೈಡ್ರೇಸ್ ಕಿಣ್ವ ಈ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಯನ್ನು ವೇಗಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: At rest the heart pumps about 5000 mL of blood per minute. If every 100 mL of oxygenated blood delivers 5 mL of O2 to the tissues, how much O2 reaches the tissues per minute? How much CO2 returns to the lungs if every 100 mL of deoxygenated blood delivers 4 mL of CO2?

steps.en: O2 delivered = 50 × 5 mL = 250 mL per minute.
CO2 delivered to the alveoli = 50 × 4 mL = 200 mL per minute.

answer.en: About 250 mL O2 per minute to the tissues and about 200 mL CO2 per minute to the lungs

narration.en: Let us work this out together. At rest the heart pumps about 5000 mL of blood per minute. If every 100 mL of oxygenated blood delivers 5 mL of O2 to the tissues, how much O2 reaches the tissues per minute? How much CO2 returns to the lungs if every 100 mL of deoxygenated blood delivers 4 mL of CO2?

say.en: Let us work this out together. At rest the heart pumps about 5000 millilitres of blood per minute. If every 100 millilitres of oxygenated blood delivers 5 millilitres of O2 to the tissues, how much O2 reaches the tissues per minute? How much CO2 returns to the lungs if every 100 millilitres of deoxygenated blood delivers 4 millilitres of CO2?
Number of 100 millilitres portions equals 5000 divided by 100 equals 50.
O2 delivered equals 50 times 5 millilitres equals 250 millilitres per minute.
CO2 delivered to the alveoli equals 50 times 4 millilitres equals 200 millilitres per minute.
So the answer is About 250 millilitres O2 per minute to the tissues and about 200 millilitres CO2 per minute to the lungs.

points.kn: ಸುಮಾರು 97% O2 ಆಕ್ಸಿಹಿಮೋಗ್ಲೋಬಿನ್ ಆಗಿ ಸಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಒಂದು ಹಿಮೋಗ್ಲೋಬಿನ್ ನಾಲ್ಕು O2 ವರೆಗೆ ಹೊರುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: The oxygen dissociation curve is sigmoid.
About 70% of CO2 travels as bicarbonate, helped by carbonic anhydrase.
points.kn: ಸುಮಾರು 70% CO2 ಕಾರ್ಬಾನಿಕ್ ಅನ್‌ಹೈಡ್ರೇಸ್ ಸಹಾಯದಿಂದ ಬೈಕಾರ್ಬನೇಟ್ ಆಗಿ ಸಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: 100 mL of blood delivers about 5 mL O2 to tissues and 4 mL CO2 to alveoli.
points.kn: 100 ಮಿ.ಲೀ ರಕ್ತ ಅಂಗಾಂಶಗಳಿಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು 5 ಮಿ.ಲೀ O2 ಮತ್ತು ಗಾಳಿಗೂಡುಗಳಿಗೆ 4 ಮಿ.ಲೀ CO2 ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: Recap. About 97% of O2 travels as oxyhaemoglobin; one Hb carries up to four O2. The oxygen dissociation curve is sigmoid. About 70% of CO2 travels as bicarbonate, helped by carbonic anhydrase. 100 mL of blood delivers about 5 mL O2 to tissues and 4 mL CO2 to alveoli.
